title: 2027-07-15 Summer Helm & Operating Reset
summary: Leadership reviewed a short-term operating reset: hiring prioritization, runway preservation, product go-to-market shifts, and reliability investments. Announced a modest hiring pause, refocus on Dedicated/Private revenue plays, APAC region expansion sequencing, and clearer SLAs for reliability. Questions covered headcount, compensation, product timelines and support for impacted teams.
action_items: Rhea Alvarez: Publish engineering priority doc with sprint reallocation by 2027-07-20
Liam O'Neal: Share updated product roadmap (Q3 reprioritized) and customer-facing note by 2027-07-19
Samir Patel: Finance to circulate runway model and hiring thresholds by 2027-07-18
Nora Kim: People to run manager 1:1 guideline and compensation FAQ by 2027-07-22
Maya Singh: Ops to publish incident RCAs for May/June reliability events by 2027-07-21
next_steps: Town-hall follow up doc and FAQ to be sent company-wide
Team-level re-prioritization workshops scheduled the week of 2027-07-19
Office hours with leadership to address compensation questions (signup link to be shared)
transcript:
Header: 2027-07-15 16:00 UTC — Duration 72 minutes — Attendees: Jordan Park, Maya Singh, Liam O'Neal, Rhea Alvarez, Samir Patel, Nora Kim + company-wide livestream

[00:00] Jordan Park (CEO): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is, uh, the summer helm and operating reset — we called it a reset because we want to be very explicit about priorities for the next 90 days. I know these words can sound heavy, but the goal is focus not fear.

[00:28] Jordan Park: Quick agenda — runway and finance context (Samir), product priorities (Liam), engineering and reliability (Rhea and Maya), people implications (Nora), then Q&A. We'll be honest and we'll follow up with docs.

[01:15] Samir Patel (CFO): Thanks Jordan. High level — we extended runway but growth has softened, so we are instituting a modest hiring pause except for mission-critical roles. We're also rebalancing spend toward revenue-facing go-to-market like Dedicated and Private. I'm happy to share the model after.

[02:05] Unidentified voice: Is this a full freeze or selective?

[02:12] Samir Patel: Selective. Critical roles and customer-impact hires will continue, but we need approvals for new reqs via a tighter rubric. We'll publish the thresholds.

[03:00] Liam O'Neal (Head of Product): On product — we are shifting staff away from exploratory projects into Optimize, Dedicated ramp, and Private deployments. Q3 will be about execution: shipping the Optimize recommendations, tightening batching and quantization suggestions, and closing a few Dedicated pilot contracts. The roadmap dates will move slightly.

[04:10] Maya Singh (CTO): On reliability — we had two notable incidents in May and June tied to autoscale and a kernel regression in one optimized runtime path. We're investing in observability, more SLO guardrails, and a second on-call rotation to reduce fatigue. We'll also add stricter release gating.

[05:05] Rhea Alvarez (VP Eng): Practically, some feature teams will be asked to pause new bets and contribute to stability sprints. We'll coordinate with product on prioritization. If your team is impacted we'll notify managers this week.

[06:00] Nora Kim (Head of People): For people — we will not be doing broad layoffs; instead a hiring pause and redeployment where possible. We know compensation conversations will come up; managers will get materials and office hours. We will support transitions if roles are sunset.

[07:10] Jordan Park: A few strategic notes — prioritize customer revenue paths (Dedicated, Private) while keeping hosted product competitive. APAC launch is still on the plan, but we'll stage it to align with Dedicated contracts in region.

[08:00] Anonymous typed question from chat: What about credits and current POCs?

[08:07] Liam O'Neal: POCs remain prioritized if they map directly to revenue. We'll continue to support existing pilots and complete contractual obligations. New exploratory POCs will be evaluated more tightly.

[09:20] Speaker 7 (Engineering): Can you clarify what "mission-critical" means for hiring?

[09:28] Samir Patel: Mission-critical equals customer-impacting revenue roles, security/compliance work needed for contracts, and roles that unblock high-probability deals. We'll publish the rubric.

[10:45] Maya Singh: Quick tech update on kernel regression — the patch rolled to canary yesterday and looks good. We're stabilizing that path and improving test coverage for quantized models. There was some noisy telemetry so apologies to teams affected by the rollback.

[12:05] Jordan Park: On transparency — we'll start weekly reliability dashboards visible to all of engineering and product. Also per-route latency SLOs and token-cost slices in Redwood Console will be surfaced.

[13:30] Rhea Alvarez: Regarding headcount realignment — some teams will see temporary reassignment to platform reliability work. We'll try to keep rotations short and purposeful. If you disagree with the reassignment, escalate to your manager and to Nora.

[15:00] Q&A (mixed): Questions about promotions/cycle timeline, recruiting pipeline, equity refreshes. Nora: Promotion cycles continue but timing may shift. Compensation committee will meet ASAP.

[16:40] Jordan Park: We also want to double-down on metrics for success: 95th pct latency targets, committed ARR from Dedicated/Private deals, and unit-cost per token improvements. Those will be the north star for decisions.

[18:10] External question from EU office: APAC region — what is the rollout plan?

[18:20] Liam O'Neal: We'll sequence APAC launch after we prove Dedicated capacity economics; likely a phased region release with a partner first. We'll share schedule in the next roadmap doc.

[19:50] Employee: Will hiring pause affect interns and IC growth?

[20:00] Nora Kim: Intern programs are moving forward for products that have active customer projects. For other programs we'll assess case-by-case. We want to protect early talent where possible.

[21:30] Jordan Park: Cultural note — leaders should be candid in team meetings, but avoid scaremongering. We will overcommunicate and provide Q&A.

[22:15] Samir Patel: On runway math — we project positive operating leverage if we reduce non-recurring spend and delay some hires. This buys us flexibility into next year. I'll send the model.

[24:00] Technical brief (Maya): We will introduce release gating: CI metrics, pre-prod latency smoke, and a rollback playbook. Also adding a second on-call rotation to reduce MTTD for incidents.

[26:00] Rhea Alvarez: For teams contributing to reliability, we'll add short-term recognition and a small bonus budget to acknowledge the work.

[27:15] Employee question: How long is the pause expected?

[27:25] Samir Patel: Tentatively 60–90 days for the strictest limits, with rolling reviews. We'll open up roles when the metrics show traction.

[28:45] Jordan Park: Ok, let's take some live questions from the chat and then open mic — we'll call for manager office hours after.

[29:10] Live Q&A — misc questions about travel budgets, all-hands cadence, mental health support. Nora: We will keep the EAP and flexible time policies, and we are exploring additional mental health resources.

[33:00] Jordan Park: Final remarks — this is about focus and durability. We built a great product and a strong team. Short-term choices don't change long-term ambition. Expect concrete follow-ups and please read the FAQ when it lands.

[34:15] Closeout: Action items recap and thanks. Leadership stays on for small-group office hours.

[35:00] (end of recording)
